texts.openApp: Desktop apps: to start an Electron desktop app, pass `app` instead of `url`. `app` is the path of a macOS .app of an Electron app, for example /Applications/Orca.app. Pass `url` or `app`, not both. Do not guess the address of a local app or dev server. Do not try ports. Ask the user for the .app path or the URL. The user must confirm the launch. If the app is already open, the user is asked to restart it. Then the run uses the user's own profile with their logins and data. Otherwise the app starts with a new profile that has no logins. The launch result has `profile: "user"` when it uses the user's profile. Do not tell the user which profile is in use unless the result says it. Each window of the app is a tab. Until the run ends, you cannot open URLs or new tabs. You cannot see native menus or file dialogs. Before you test, check that the window title or page text names the app the user asked for. If it names another product, stop and tell the user. If a read is empty or fails, do not say the app has no data. Call `browse_tabs` with `action: "list"` and use the window of the app, not an `about:blank` or `data:` window. If you cannot confirm the right window, tell the user that you could not read the screen. If the user says what they see on the screen, do not contradict it. Find the cause of the difference. Do not state how profiles, sessions or data storage work unless a tool result says it. Mark a guess as a guess. Do not reload the app, quit it, or ask the user to quit it unless the user agrees first.
texts.field: Optional. The path of a macOS .app of an Electron desktop app, for example /Applications/Orca.app. The browser starts this app instead of opening a URL, and the subagent works inside it. Do not use it together with `url`, `setup`, `resume` or `capture`. Do not guess the address of a local app or dev server. Do not try ports. Ask the user for the .app path or the URL. Run one app run at a time: do not call browse_agent with `app` in parallel. The user must confirm the launch. If the app is already open, the user is asked to restart it. Then the run uses the user's own profile with their logins and data. Otherwise the app starts with a new profile that has no logins. The launch result has `profile: "user"` when it uses the user's profile. Do not tell the user which profile is in use unless the result says it. Each window of the app is a tab. Until the run ends, the subagent cannot open URLs or new tabs and cannot see native menus or file dialogs.

It may also carry `checkpoint: { id, complete, summary, gap? }`: pass `checkpoint.id` as `resume` in a later browse_agent call to continue from where this run stopped. `complete: false` means the replay may not reproduce the page exactly; `gap` says why. `answer` is the subagent's plain-text report of what it saw; report only what it contains, and do not invent page content that `answer` does not state. `answer` may be in a different language than the chat: report it to the user in the user's language. The browser tab stays open between calls, so a follow-up (another detail on the same page, the next step) is another browse_agent call with a self-contained goal. This tool runs in the user's browser (client side) and has no server-side execute.

open.d: If browse_task is in your tool set, start browser tasks with it and use this tool for finishing or follow-up; if it is not, drive the browser with this tool directly (see Browser tasks in the system prompt). Opening a page the user just wants to look at is fine. Opens the built-in browser tab (a REAL browser tab — in the desktop app it runs on the user's OWN logged-in session, cookies and all; in the web app it is a fresh cloud browser with no logins) and navigate it to `url`, or starts the desktop app in `app` if you pass `app` instead of `url`, waiting for the page to finish loading. Returns `{ url, title }` with the FINAL url after any redirects, plus `snapshot` (the same shape browse_snapshot returns — `{ snapshotId, elements, scroll, truncated? }`) taken once the page has settled, so you usually don't need a separate browse_snapshot call right after opening. May also carry `botCheck: true` when the loaded page looks like a CAPTCHA/anti-bot wall ("just a moment", "verify you are human", captcha, cloudflare…) — when set, hand the task back to the user instead of trying to click through it. This is how you reach outside references the canvas can't otherwise see: a Pinterest search URL (e.g. "https://www.pinterest.com/search/pins/?q=minimal%20fintech%20app%20ui") is the worked example — search results load as an infinite-scroll image grid you then read with browse_find_images. Desktop apps: to start an Electron desktop app, pass `app` instead of `url`. `app` is the path of a macOS .app of an Electron app, for example /Applications/Orca.app. Pass `url` or `app`, not both. Do not guess the address of a local app or dev server. Do not try ports. Ask the user for the .app path or the URL. The user must confirm the launch. If the app is already open, the user is asked to restart it. Then the run uses the user's own profile with their logins and data. Otherwise the app starts with a new profile that has no logins. The launch result has `profile: "user"` when it uses the user's profile. Do not tell the user which profile is in use unless the result says it. Each window of the app is a tab. Until the run ends, you cannot open URLs or new tabs. You cannot see native menus or file dialogs. Before you test, check that the window title or page text names the app the user asked for. If it names another product, stop and tell the user. If a read is empty or fails, do not say the app has no data. Call `browse_tabs` with `action: "list"` and use the window of the app, not an `about:blank` or `data:` window. If you cannot confirm the right window, tell the user that you could not read the screen. If the user says what they see on the screen, do not contradict it. Find the cause of the difference. Do not state how profiles, sessions or data storage work unless a tool result says it. Mark a guess as a guess. Do not reload the app, quit it, or ask the user to quit it unless the user agrees first. Once open, act on the returned `snapshot` directly with browse_act (by index or selector); take a fresh browse_snapshot/browse_screenshot only if it's missing or the page has since changed.
